reports.title: H World Group Limited Reports Third Quarter of 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

guidance.heading: Guidance
section: We have raised our guidance for the full year of 2026, now expecting Group revenue growth to be in the range of 9%-10% compared to the full year of 2025, up from our previous guidance of 4%-8%, of which HWC revenue growth to be in the range of 13%-14% compared to the previous guidance of 7%-11%. H World now expects its M&F revenue growth to be in the range of 22%-23% compared to the full year of 2025, and up from our previous guidance of 16%-20%.
The above forecast reflects the Company’s current and preliminary view, which is subject to change.

desk.headline: Revenue up 11% to RMB7.75bn, beat; full-year revenue growth guidance raised to 9–10% from 4–8%
results: Revenue rose 11.3% to RMB7.75bn, ahead of the RMB7.33bn estimate, driven by 25.7% growth in fees from franchised and managed hotels.
Revenue from company-run hotels fell 7.4% as H World keeps exiting leases, and the international arm shrank 7.7% after European closures.
Adjusted EPS rose to RMB6.23 per ADS from RMB4.76, beating the RMB5.60 estimate; operating margin widened to 33.2%.
China room prices rose 1.8% but occupancy slipped to 82.6%, leaving RevPAR flat; same-hotel RevPAR fell 4.4%.
The network reached 14,026 hotels after 664 openings in China; net cash was RMB9.3bn.

guidance.summary: H World raised its 2026 targets: group revenue growth to 9–10% (was 4–8%), China revenue growth to 13–14% (was 7–11%) and franchised and managed revenue growth to 22–23% (was 16–20%).

points: The CEO said Q4 demand is slightly better than expected, and full-year RevPAR is still seen up slightly.
Travel held up over the October holidays, with some recovery in business trips around trade fairs.
More hotels than planned will close this year as part of a two-year quality clean-up; franchisees are signing more selectively.
Margins may swing near term as it invests in brands, membership, technology and overseas growth.
Management restated its commitment to shareholder returns but gave no new dividend or buyback figures, and no 2027 targets.

watch: Whether same-hotel RevPAR in China stops falling.
Hotel openings against the 2,200–2,300 full-year target, and the pace of closures.
Any 2027 guidance and new shareholder-return plans with Q4 results.
